task.description: Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for docs/issues/ISS-0047.yaml, on branch feature/WF03-ISS0047-20260818. ISS-0047: Letflow.Identity.insert_or_fetch/4 (lib/letflow/identity.ex) issues Repo.insert(changeset, on_conflict: :nothing, conflict_target: {:unsafe_fragment, "(external_realm, external_id) WHERE external_id IS NOT NULL"}, ...). This only suppresses a conflict on the users_external_identity_partial_index. users also carries unique_index(:users, [:username]). Two genuinely independent Postgres connections racing to insert the same (external_realm, external_id) AND the same username can have the losing insert raise {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{username: ["has already been taken"]}} instead of resolving to the same row both callers expect via re_select_on_conflict/3. Reproduced deterministically (3/3 runs) by TEST-DESIGNER during REQ-063 using :auto sandbox mode (genuine independent connections) instead of the original :manual mode + Sandbox.allow/3 (which serializes both inserts onto one connection and never exercises this path). Full history in docs/issues/ISS-0047.yaml.
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5: search docs/issues/*.yaml with status: resolved for a prior matching fix; state in the handoff summary whether a match was found (expected: none, this is a pre-existing REQ-018 gap never fixed before).

Step 1: reproduce the race directly against real Postgres (two independent connections, not Sandbox :manual mode) and confirm the actual {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} output — do not diagnose from the issue report's prose alone.

Trace to root cause: confirm on_conflict's conflict_target covers only the external_realm/external_id partial index, not the separate username unique index, and confirm which of the two racing inserts is affected.
Write diagnosis into result.summary: root cause, affected files/functions, and what a fix needs to change (do NOT implement the fix).
Set next_action to 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design'.

result.summary:
Step 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml (48 entries) for 'identity', 'conflict_target', 'username' — 9 files matched (ISS-0002, 0005, 0006, 0007, 0031, 0032, 0040, 0047, 0048), all either docs/design-doc issues or unrelated flakiness/cleanup issues (e.g. ISS-0031 is a different flaky-assertion issue in tenant_status_test.exs, ISS-0048 is orphaned-schema cleanup). None concern insert_or_fetch/4's on_conflict/conflict_target logic or a username-uniqueness race. No prior resolved entry matches this symptom — confirmed this is a first occurrence, not a recurrence. No severity flag-up needed.

Step 1 (diagnose, reproduced directly): Wrote a standalone scratch ExUnit file (scratch/repro_iss0047_test.exs, deleted after use, not committed) that provisions a real tenant schema via Letflow.TenantProvisioning, then races two Task.async/1-spawned processes — each barrier-synchronized to call Identity.provision_oidc_user/4 at effectively the same instant — under Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox :auto mode for BOTH the provisioning step and the race itself (genuinely independent Postgres connections per task, unlike the checked-in identity_test.exs's :manual + Sandbox.allow/3 mechanism which the moduledoc itself documents as serializing both inserts onto one shared connection and never exercising this path). Ran it 6 times against the real test Postgres (localhost:5462, MIX_TEST_PARTITION=99) with identical (external_realm, external_id) AND identical username across both racing calls. Result: 4 of 6 runs produced exactly the failure ISS-0047 predicts — one of the two Task results was {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} with errors_on giving %{username: ["has already been taken"]}, raised directly from Repo.insert/2 inside insert_or_fetch/4 (lib/letflow/identity.ex line ~188-218), not from any application-level conflict handling; the OTHER task's call succeeded with created: true. In the 2/6 runs that did not hit the bug, both calls resolved cleanly (one created: true, one created: false) — consistent with this being a genuine, timing-dependent Postgres-level race (not deterministic every time, unlike TEST-DESIGNER's report of 3/3 — the non-determinism itself is corroborating evidence this is a real cross-connection race, not an artifact of a specific harness setup). Confirmed exactly one row ever exists afterward regardless (ROW COUNT: 1 in every run) — the DATA ends up consistent, but one of the two CALLERS receives a hard {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} instead of the {:ok, %{user: _, created: false}} provision_oidc_user/4's own @doc promises ('Always returns {:error, reason} on failure — never raises on a realistic failure path', listing only JIT-disabled/changeset-validation/conflict-race-fallback as expected failure reasons; an application-visible username-collision error caused purely by opponent-task timing is not one of those and is a genuine caller-visible contract violation).

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not guessed): lib/letflow/identity.ex, insert_or_fetch/4 (lines 174-219). The Repo.insert/2 call at lines 188-194 passes on_conflict: :nothing with conflict_target: {:unsafe_fragment, "(external_realm, external_id) WHERE external_id IS NOT NULL"} — this ON CONFLICT arbiter names ONLY the users_external_identity_partial_index. Postgres's ON CONFLICT machinery only suppresses/no-ops a conflict detected against the NAMED arbiter index; per Postgres's own documented INSERT ... ON CONFLICT semantics, a conflict on ANY OTHER unique index not named as the arbiter (here, unique_index(:users, [:username]), defined in the same users table/migration but never referenced by this on_conflict clause) is NOT suppressible by that ON CONFLICT clause at all and raises the underlying unique-violation as a normal constraint error, which Ecto surfaces as the {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} at line 216-217 of insert_or_fetch/4 (that clause was written only to catch ordinary changeset-validation failures — e.g. a pre-existing username collision from an UNRELATED identity — not this race). Because REQ-018's own concurrent-race acceptance-criterion-3 test (test/letflow/identity_test.exs lines 259-355) always used :manual mode + Sandbox.allow/3 (both Tasks sharing one physical connection/transaction, confirmed by that test's own inline comments and moduledoc lines 54-64), the two INSERT attempts were always serialized at the Postgres session level before a genuine cross-connection race on BOTH indexes simultaneously could ever be exercised — so this gap was never caught by REQ-018's original test, and is not a REQ-063 regression (REQ-063 only threaded prefix: opts through, per docs/issues/ISS-0047.yaml's own account, confirmed correct by reading identity.ex — no on_conflict/conflict_target lines were touched by REQ-063).

AFFECTED FILES/FUNCTIONS: lib/letflow/identity.ex — insert_or_fetch/4 (lines 174-219), specifically the Repo.insert/2 call's on_conflict/conflict_target opts (lines 188-194) and the {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} passthrough branch (lines 216-217) which currently cannot distinguish 'a genuine pre-existing username collision from a different identity' (a real, permanent error that should propagate) from 'this specific race's opponent-task got there first with the same identity AND same username' (which should resolve via re_select_on_conflict/3, same as the (external_realm, external_id) conflict path already does at lines 210-214).

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE (shape only, not designed — CODE-DESIGNER's job): the {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} branch (or the on_conflict clause itself) needs to distinguish this specific race outcome from a genuine collision, then fall through to re_select_on_conflict/3 for the race case. This likely means: (a) inspecting the returned changeset's errors for specifically a username unique-constraint violation (Ecto tags this via unique_constraint/changeset internals — Repo.insert/2's error changeset carries a constraint-type-tagged error the code can pattern-match rather than a generic string), and only then re-querying via get_by_external_identity/3 (same helper re_select_on_conflict/3 already uses) to check whether the row that now exists for THIS (external_realm, external_id) triple is the losing caller's own conflict partner (i.e., the SAME identity that this call itself was trying to provision) — if so, resolve to {:ok, %{user: existing, created: false}} same as the existing on_conflict path; if the existing username-holder is a genuinely different (external_realm, external_id) than what this call is provisioning, that is a real, unrelated collision and must still propagate as {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} as it does today (this is exactly what identity_test.exs's REQ-063 'two users with the same username in the SAME tenant schema' test at lines 379-394 already pins and must keep passing). CODE-DESIGNER should also consider whether Postgres offers a single-statement alternative (e.g. a second ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT clause is not supported by Postgres — only one arbiter per INSERT — so a chained/fallback-query approach as above, or an explicit advisory lock around the whole select-then-insert sequence, are the realistic options) and must design the corresponding new independent-two-connection test (promoting this issue's own :auto-mode repro shape) since identity_test.exs's current acceptance-criterion-3 test does not and structurally cannot exercise this path under :manual mode.

next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design.
